Doesn't have to happen right away because I think it would be good to get a little bit of buy-in on one more draft spec, after which getting a draft EIP written up for this is probably the logical next step cc <@!425615769280315392> ^ access lists (for provable WIT protocol stuff for beam sync) hi all, I am working on wit/0 implementation for ethereumjs-client and i was wondering if there are any tests that would help confirm our witness collection is correct. for example a blockchain of 5-10 blocks with the witnesses of each would be really helpful to ensure our implementation is consistent, or if there is any other suggestions that would be great! Nope, I don't think there are any test cases published. It's worth noting that `wit/0` is not intended to be consensus-sensitive. ie~ it's ideal to report exactly the same hashes, but it's not critical. One straightforward way to test is by executing a block against only the state identified by the hashes in `wit/0`, and see if it completes successfully. If you want to send me a witness (hashes and bodies) against a recent mainnet block, I'd be happy to check if it matches the py-evm implementation. great thanks for the explanation, yeah having some results for mainnet blocks might be nice, I’ll let you know 🙂

excerpts.author: r.alxz
excerpts.content: hi all, I am working on wit/0 implementation for ethereumjs-client and i was wondering if there are any tests that would help confirm our witness collection is correct. for example a blockchain of 5-10 blocks with the witnesses of each would be really helpful to ensure our implementation is consistent, or if there is any other suggestions that would be great!

excerpts.author: jason.carver
excerpts.content:
Nope, I don't think there are any test cases published. It's worth noting that `wit/0` is not intended to be consensus-sensitive. ie~ it's ideal to report exactly the same hashes, but it's not critical. One straightforward way to test is by executing a block against only the state identified by the hashes in `wit/0`, and see if it completes successfully.
If you want to send me a witness (hashes and bodies) against a recent mainnet block, I'd be happy to check if it matches the py-evm implementation.
